newsitem.title: UK: N.Electric sees yr profits over 112 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: N.Electric sees yr profits over 112 mln stg.

text.p: British regional electricity company Northern Electric, subject of a hostile bid from CE Electric, said pretax profits for the year ending March 31 would be over 112 million pounds ($188 million), with a dividend of 29.85 pence.
It said gearing at that date should be around 95 percent after paying out a special dividend commmitted as part of a package used to fend off Trafalgar House, now part of Kvaerner, last year.

The company, which has said it is undervalued by CE Electric's 630 pence per share offer, reported half year pretax profits of 50.7 million pounds and paid out a dividend of 12.85 pence, while its interim gearing stood at 47 percent.

Northern said gearing without the special dividend, which would lapse if CE Electric won control, would be roughly in line with other electricity companies and argued that based on 1997 forecast cash flow, it should be valued at 745 pence.

CE Electric, which is 70 percent owned by CalEnergy of the U.S., has already bought nearly 30 percent of Northern as the company's share price languishes around 600 pence because of concerns that the UK government might block its bid.
Northern said CE Electric indicated a price of 700 pence in talks before it launched the $1.225 billion bid on October 28, but the American company has consistently denied the claim. ($1=.5956 Pound)
